b: Orders for Italian woodworking technology rose by 1.2% year on year in the third quarter of 2026, slowing from the previous quarter. Companies remain cautious about demand in the months ahead, according to Acimall’s latest survey.
Order index for woodworking technologies in the third quarter of 2026 (Image: Acimall)

The Italian woodworking and furniture technology industry continued to face subdued demand in the third quarter of 2026, with order growth slowing amid persistent weakness in domestic and international markets.

According to an economic survey by Acimall’s studies office, total orders increased by 1.2% in Jul-Sep 2026 compared with the same period in 2025. This was down from the 5.3% year-on-year growth recorded in the second quarter.

Foreign orders for Italian-made products rose by 1.7%, compared with 12.3% in Apr-Jun. Domestic orders, meanwhile, fell by 0.7% year on year, although this was an improvement on the 12.3% decline recorded in the previous quarter.
The order backlog stood at 3.6 months, up slightly from 3.5 months in the second quarter. Prices also increased, rising by 4.3% since the beginning of 2026, compared with 3.5% as of the end of Jun.

The survey’s assessment of current business conditions presented a mixed picture. Some 24% of respondents reported an increase in production, up from 18% in the previous quarter. Meanwhile, 41% reported stable production, down from 59%, while 35% reported a decline, compared with 23% in Apr-Jun.

Employment levels remained largely unchanged, with 88% of companies reporting stable staffing levels. The remaining respondents were evenly split, with 6% reporting an increase and 6% a decrease. Available stocks were also stable for 65% of companies, while 18% reported an increase and 17% a reduction.
Expectations for the remaining months of 2026 remain cautious. For domestic orders, 65% of respondents expect conditions to remain stable, while 23% anticipate a decline and 12% forecast growth.
For foreign orders, expectations are somewhat more mixed. Some 53% of companies expect demand to remain stable, while 18% anticipate an increase and 29% expect a decline.
